number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 477A & 120B IPC and Section 13(1) C/D read with 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. Final upheld: Not stated
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the criminal trial involving offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act must be conducted and concluded at the earliest.
witness_credibility: The court assessed that the applicant (respondent No.2) was not connected with the criminal proceeding and had no locus standi to file the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 09.01.2006; Trial judgment: 23.05.2020; High Court decision: 09.09.2020; Supreme Court decision: 16.12.2020
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Not stated; Counsel for the State: Not stated
investigation_status: FIR registered on 09.01.2006; Charge sheet filed on 23.05.2020; Trial completed: Not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: Not stated; High Court: Order dated 09.09.2020; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, High Court order set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that criminal trials involving offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act must be conducted and concluded at the earliest to ensure justice is delivered to the accused if found guilty.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court erred in entertaining the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. filed by respondent No.2, who had no locus standi to challenge the criminal proceedings.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that criminal trials involving offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act must be expedited, and that third parties cannot raise issues under the garb of Public Interest Litigation.
precedent_relied_upon: Janata Dal v. H.S. Chowdhary and Others (1993) 1 SCC 756
